exposure.note: Measured from the compose files, not asserted. pod_internal is expose-only; a published port is what makes a surface pod_external.
exposure.evidence: Measured 2026-09-05 from the deployment files, per rule 4. runtimes/mind-pod/docker-compose.yml publishes ONE port: line 102, service config, "127.0.0.1:13003:3000". runtimes/mind-pod/app/extract/compose.yml publishes three: line 34 back, line 79 front, line 111 config, all 127.0.0.1. Every other service is expose-only. oxigraph binds 0.0.0.0:7878 INSIDE the pod network and has no ports: entry, so it is not host-published. Every publication names a loopback host, so these surfaces are reachable from the host and not from the open internet -- which is what pod_external means. Held by tooling/compose/check_loopback_publish.py. A published port is what makes a surface pod_external rather than pod_internal, so the services absent from that list are the pod-internal ones. Until 2026-09-05 those four ports named no host interface, so Docker bound 0.0.0.0 and they were reachable from wherever the host was, while this field asserted loopback. The addresses were added and the assertion became a measurement.

invariants: callers allowlisted per seam (*_CALLERS), Bearer tokens
